title: Humans and AI respond similarly to task difficulty when reasoning about content moderation dilemmas
abstract: arXiv:2508.20262v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) generate intermediate reasoning steps before producing answers, improving performance on challenging problems by iteratively developing solutions. There is evidence that LRMs expend more effort on the problems that take people longer to solve, but it is unclear whether these relationships hold on more subjective tasks without verifiable answers. This study addresses this issue through an experiment using a content moderation task, where task difficulty is manipulated by varying the relative offensiveness of two different options. Comparing six large reasoning models with 1,854 human subjects, we find that models expend more reasoning effort, measured using the length of the chain-of-thought (CoT), on the kinds of cases that take people longer to adjudicate. translated_title: 人类与AI在推理内容审核难题时对任务难度的反应相似
translated_abstract: 大型推理模型（LRMs）在生成最终答案之前会先产生中间推理步骤，通过迭代地完善解决方案来提升其在具有挑战性问题上的表现。已有证据表明，LRMs会在那些人们需要更长时间才能解决的问题上投入更多努力，但这种关系是否适用于没有可验证答案的更为主观的任务尚不明确。本研究通过一项内容审核任务的实验来探讨这一问题，实验通过改变两个不同选项之间的相对冒犯程度来操纵任务难度。通过将六个大型推理模型与1,854名人类受试者进行对比，我们发现模型在那些人们需要更长时间裁决的案例上会付出更多的推理努力（以思维链CoT的长度来衡量）。当两篇帖子的冒犯程度持平时，人们的判断时间延长了31%，而模型生成的思维链长度则增加了51%至306%。
tldr: 本研究通过内容审核实验发现，大型推理模型在更难的主观判断任务上会投入更多推理努力（思维链更长），其努力程度与人类所花时间呈现出相似的相关模式。
en_tdlr: This study finds that large reasoning models expend more reasoning effort (longer chain-of-thought) on harder subjective content moderation tasks, mirroring the relationship between task difficulty and human response time.
